segments.text: > Part of the [Implementation Status](README.md) index. Real OS threads and cross-thread messaging.

caveats: One listener per event, arrow-function literals only
One message type per direction, declared by annotation

Payloads: structured-clone-safe values only (plus `SharedArrayBuffer`/`MessagePort`, which cross by reference — [ADR-00308](../adr/ADR-00308.md)/[ADR-00309](../adr/ADR-00309.md)); strings share their buffer across threads; no arrays through `onmessage`/`e.data`
`'error'` carries the message string, not an Error object; no `self.onerror`
`terminate()` is cooperative, keeps queued messages, always exits 1
Worker path must be a string literal; a worker module can't also be imported, can't spawn workers, and its named functions can't read its own top-level bindings
`-mm=manual` leaks per message; no combining with `http.listen({workers:N})`
notes: Two surfaces: Node `worker_threads` and the browser `Worker`/`onmessage` shape ([TDD-00098](../tdd/TDD-00098.md), [ADR-00305](../adr/ADR-00305.md), [ADR-00306](../adr/ADR-00306.md))
The worker file compiles into the same binary as its own entry function
Each thread runs its own event loop (runtime singletons are `thread_local`); messages travel over pipes as pointer envelopes, deep-copied at the boundary
`-mm=gc` registers each thread with Boehm
Uncaught worker exception → `'error'` + `'exit'(1)` on the parent, or process exit if unhandled
darwin/arm64 and Linux (glibc/arm64, Docker) both verified across the whole worker suite, including `-mm=gc` ([ADR-00351](../adr/ADR-00351.md)). `--static` + `-pthread` recheck still pending

caveats: Channel name must be a string literal; one message type per channel name, program-wide (first `postMessage` or annotated `onmessage` fixes it)
`onmessage` property only (arrow-function literal, `(e: { data: T })`); no `addEventListener`, no `'messageerror'`
Array payloads not supported through `onmessage`
`close()` leaks the endpoint's two pipe fds by design (closes a race against an in-flight post)
`-mm=manual` leaks per delivery (payload ownership passes to the listener)
notes: Process-wide name-keyed registry; each subscriber gets its own deep copy (codegen-synthesized clone thunk, called once per subscriber); delivery rides each thread's `select()` loop over per-endpoint pipes ([TDD-00099](../tdd/TDD-00099.md), [ADR-00309](../adr/ADR-00309.md))
A registered `onmessage` holds its thread's loop alive until `close()` (Node ref semantics)
Works same-thread and across workers
verified on darwin/arm64 and Linux (glibc/arm64, Docker)

caveats: Message type fixed at construction (`new MessageChannel<T>()`, default `number`), symmetric for both ports

A port crosses a worker boundary only whole — as `workerData` or as the entire `postMessage` payload — and is **shared, not neutered**: the sender must stop using a sent port (unsynchronized use from two threads is memory-safe but unordered); the `MessageChannel` pair box itself never crosses
`onmessage` property only (arrow literal); no `on('message')`, no `start()`/`'close'` event, no array payloads via `onmessage`
`close()` leaks two pipe fds; `-mm=manual` leaks per message
notes: Importable under Node's module name too — `import { MessageChannel/MessagePort/BroadcastChannel } from 'worker_threads'` ([ADR-00431](../adr/ADR-00431.md))

One shared endpoint runtime with `BroadcastChannel` (pipe per endpoint, peer-linked halves); a port is drained by whichever thread registered its `onmessage` — no adoption protocol needed when a port moves to a worker ([TDD-00099](../tdd/TDD-00099.md), [ADR-00309](../adr/ADR-00309.md))
`postMessage` into a closed peer silently discards, matching spec
Verified same-thread, port-as-`workerData`, and port-as-`postMessage`-payload round trips (darwin/arm64 and Linux glibc/arm64, Docker)

caveats: Channel ops are synchronous blocking (`ch.send(v)`/`ch.receive()`), not `await`; element is a fixed 8-byte slot (number/string/object/boolean)

`select` cases are `ch.recvCase(v => …)` / `ch.sendCase(x, () => …)` / `defaultCase(() => …)`; a recv handler receives the value but not the closed flag (use `for (const v of ch)` range, which ends on close, to detect it)

Fixed goroutine stacks (default 256 KiB, tunable via `KLAINSYNC_STACK_KB`), no overflow guard — deep recursion is UB; true growable/moving stacks are gated on precise stack maps ([TDD-00135](../tdd/TDD-00135.md))

Blocking-syscall P-handoff is a bounded sysmon-driven rescue-M approximation, not full `entersyscall`/`exitsyscall`; a nil (never-constructed) channel isn't expressible — channels are always `new Channel`

Per-iteration capture of a loop `let` directly in a goroutine closure is a pre-existing general closure limitation — pass the value as a function parameter (a `spawn(work)` helper) instead; a top-level channel is a module global, so a helper function sees it with its type intact
`send` after `close` and `close` of a closed channel abort the process (Go-panic parity); native-only (compile error under plain `tsc`/Node)
notes: A Go-style GMP work-stealing scheduler in the embedded C runtime `klainsyncsrc/klainsync.c`: one P + pinned M (pthread) per `GOMAXPROCS`, a global run-queue backstop, half-queue stealing, periodic global-queue poll; blocking channel send/receive parks the *goroutine*, not the OS thread ([TDD-00143](../tdd/TDD-00143.md), [ADR-00541](../adr/ADR-00541.md))

`go(() => void)` spawns; `new Channel<T>(cap)` is an unbuffered rendezvous or buffered ring with `.send`/`.receive`/`.close` and `for (const v of ch)` range; `select(...)` is Go's random-fair select over recv/send cases (`sudog` groups with an atomic winner claim) ([ADR-00543](../adr/ADR-00543.md))

Complete tier-1 cooperative preemption ([ADR-00542](../adr/ADR-00542.md)): a `sysmon` thread flags an over-budget goroutine; the compiler emits `klainsync_safepoint()` at function entry and every loop back-edge (for/while/do-while/for-of/for-in), gated on the resolver's `UsesKlainSync` flag so a program that never imports the module emits and links nothing. Signal-based async preemption is unnecessary given full loop instrumentation
Blocking-call resilience: work-stealing drains a blocked M's goroutines; when all Ms block at once, a bounded rescue M is spawned so the program doesn't deadlock
Links only when `klain:sync` is imported; `-mm=gc` registers each M and each goroutine stack with Boehm
Validated standalone (rendezvous, 100-goroutine fan-in, close-drain, select, `GOMAXPROCS=1` preemption, all-Ms-blocked rescue) clean under ThreadSanitizer; E2E on darwin/arm64
